# Best open-ear earbuds for running

**Quick pick:** The Bose Ultra Open Earbuds are the best all-around choice, and the Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 is best if you want maximum awareness. Prices below come from the linked reviews and may have changed.

## Top picks

| Need | Pick | Price | Key specs |
|---|---|---|---|
| Best overall (clip-on) | Bose Ultra Open Earbuds | $199 on sale ($299 list) | 7 hr (19.5 with case), IPX4 |
| Best bone conduction | Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 | $180 list, $125 at some retailers | 12 hr, IP55, neckband |
| Best for long or wet runs | Shokz OpenDots 2 | $200 | 10 hr (40 with case), IP57 |
| Best value | Nothing Ear (Open) | $99 (was $149) | IP54, strong bass for the category |
| Budget | JLab Flex Open | about $40-50 | 7 hr (21 with case) |

**Bose Ultra Open.** Runner's World named it best overall for its sound quality, comfort and secure fit, and the speakers are aimed at the ear canal to limit sound leakage. WIRED likes the physical buttons, which are easier to use mid-run than touch controls. Downsides are the price, the IPX4 water resistance for heavy rain, and volume that can feel low in loud traffic. Runner's World also says Bose plans to release new open-ear earbuds within about a month, so you may want to wait or watch for discounts.
- Reviews with buy links: [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/), [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Shokz OpenRun Pro 2.** This is the best choice if hearing your surroundings is the top priority. It combines bone conduction with small air-conduction speakers for fuller bass, and it has physical buttons. WIRED found its clarity a bit below the older OpenRun and the Bose. Runner's World noted the band can interfere with a low ponytail or winter hats. RTINGS says the Bose is slightly better for most people, but the Shokz has the tougher IP55 rating and won't bother you if you have ear piercings.
- Reviews with buy links: [WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/), [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)

**Shokz OpenDots 2.** WIRED's top overall pick. It has the longest battery life here, an IP57 rating (WIRED submerged them without problems), and leaves the top of your ear free for glasses and hats. It's pricey, and Runner's World notes the volume could be better.
- Reviews with buy links: [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Nothing Ear (Open).** SoundGuys picked it as best open-ear overall and best for running, with a customizable EQ and good controls. It's a strong choice at $99.
- Review with buy link: [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)

## Budget options
- **JLab Flex Open** is a low-risk way to test whether clip-ons suit you. Sound is less detailed and it has touch controls only. Runner's World lists it at $40 in one place and $50 in another. [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)
- **SoundPEATS PearlClip Pro** is WIRED's cheap pick at about $50. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)
- **Soundcore AeroFit 2** is a hook-style design with IP55, 10 hr per bud and 42 hr with the case. SoundGuys lists it at $79.99, while Dealectric lists $129.99 ($104 with code AFSC20, not tested by me). Compare prices before buying. [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/) | [Buy at Soundcore via Dealectric (affiliate link)](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-aerofit-2)

## Tips
- Open-ear earbuds leak sound and don't block noise, so they're a poor fit for gyms or flights. Keep the volume low enough to hear traffic.
- If you have long hair or wear hats a lot, choose a clip-on (Bose or OpenDots 2) over the neckband Shokz.
- For heavy rain, the OpenDots 2 (IP57) or OpenRun Pro 2 (IP55) are safer than the Bose (IPX4).

The sources didn't give me direct product-page links for most of these models, so the article links above are where the current retailer buy links are. I can narrow this down if you tell me your budget, whether you use iPhone or Android, and whether you wear glasses or hats.
